result.title: Less Than Meets the Eye: Action-Set Identifiability and Principled Abstention for 3D Physical Geometry
result.summary: A corridor, its mirror reflection, and its image on a display can look identical, yet their physical surfaces lie at different depths. We test whether bounded camera motions distinguish these explanations. Intervene3D takes an image and an initial geometry estimate, predicts the view under each hypothesis and candidate motion, and selects a motion by maximin separability. It reports the mechanism and first physical surface only if the available motions separate the hypotheses still in contention. Otherwise it abstains. An adequacy test also rejects observations that no hypothesis explains. On a matched synthetic benchmark with exact landmarks, disabling abstention gives confident answers on 76.4% of unresolvable scenes. With abstention, none receives a confident answer under exact or noisy landmarks. At 100% accuracy on answered scenes, maximin selection answers 61.0% of scenes and summed selection 43.1%. The adequacy test lowers wrong answers on strongly curved mirror scenes from 56.8% to 12.4%. Real display experiments compare two hypotheses using one frozen depth-network estimate. The second image supplies photometric evidence and is never passed through the depth network. One executed motion reduces the pooled median surface error of twelve networks by 31.5%. These networks have larger error inside the annotated panel than outside on 33.4% of illusion-benchmark images. They place the first physical surface behind the glass on 36.9% of Mirror3D frames.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Intervene3D：给定图像与初始几何估计，预测各假设（走廊、镜面、显示图像）在候选相机运动下的视图，按 maximin 可分性选择运动，仅在剩余假设可被区分时报告机制与首个物理表面，否则弃权，并附加拒绝无假设可解释观测的充分性检验；在合成与真实显示基准上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 「选动作取证据—检验证据是否足够—不可判定则弃权」的回路，可为 LVR 中何时继续获取视觉证据（LOOK）与何时停止作答（STOP）的问题表述和评价提供参照，但对象是相机运动与 3D 表面假设，迁移价值需核查。
